summary: AFL Talent Ambassador Kevin Sheehan released his top 40 prospects for the 2023 AFL Draft, profiling each player's state, clubs, height, strengths, combine results and a current-AFL-player comparison. Harley Reid is compared to Dustin Martin, Taylor Goad to Max Gawn and Will Green to Brodie Grundy. The draft is on November 20 and 21, with the rookie draft a day later.
one_line: Kevin Sheehan's top 40 prospects for the 2023 AFL Draft, with profiles, combine results and comparisons to current AFL stars.
key_facts: Kevin Sheehan is the AFL Talent Ambassador; his top 40 prospects were announced by the AFL in a press release on Thursday.
The 2023 AFL Draft is on November 20 and 21, with the rookie draft a day later, shown on Fox Footy and Kayo.
Sheehan profiled all 129 players who attended the 2023 AFL Draft Combine or State Draft Combine; the full list is on the AFL Draft Hub.
Harley Reid (Bendigo Pioneers, 187cm) is compared to Dustin Martin (Richmond); he was All Australian for the second year in a row and finished third in the Larke Medal voting.
Taylor Goad, a 206cm South Australian ruckman who previously focused on basketball, is compared to Max Gawn (Melbourne).
Will Green, a 204cm Northern Knights ruckman, is compared to Brodie Grundy (Sydney Swans).
Ryley Sanders won the Larke Medal as best and fairest at the National Championships, averaging 35 disposals, and captained the All Australian team; he is compared to Andrew Brayshaw (Fremantle).
Colby McKercher won the Coates Talent League's Morrish Medal and was runner-up in the Larke Medal; he is compared to Zac Merrett (Essendon).
Kynan Brown is eligible under the father-son rule to Melbourne as son of Nathan D Brown, who played 146 games for the Demons.
Jordan Croft (200cm) is eligible to join the Western Bulldogs under the father-son rule as son of Matthew Croft, who played 186 games, and is compared to Max King (St Kilda).
Will McCabe is eligible for Hawthorn father-son as son of Luke McCabe, who played 138 games for the Hawks from 1995 to 2004.
Jed Walter (Gold Coast Suns Academy) kicked 11 goals in four National Championships games and is expected to receive a very early bid the Suns will match; he is compared to Charlie Curnow (Carlton).
Ethan Read ran 5:56 for the 2km time trial at the national Draft Combine and won the Hunter Harrison Medal; Darcy Wilson was second in that test at 5:52.
Nick Watson (170cm) kicked 14 goals in four National Championships games for Victoria Metro to top the goalkicking and is compared to Shai Bolton (Richmond).
